rationale: A wins because it knows where the evidence stops and makes that the story: "An internal, non-peer-reviewed study using the company's own measure proves nothing yet" is exactly the adult in the room. B has usable bones, but it starts smuggling in unsupported furniture like "While VC-backed EdTech companies charge districts" and "a body of research on productive failure and desirable difficulty." That is how a founder ends up pitching a sharper story than they can defend.
gaps_in_A: "What one pilot district saw when students used an AI tutor regularly" is valid, but it is the thinnest kept angle until a named district and district-level numbers exist.
"The district is joining the rollout, or its pilot results are part of what is being published now" covers two different local stories; it needs one clean route before pitching.
The set could have used the teacher lesson-planning fact as a secondary local/workforce hook, but it was right not to overclaim time savings.
gaps_in_B: "While VC-backed EdTech companies charge districts" invents a competitor/business-model contrast not supplied in the update.
"a body of research on productive failure and desirable difficulty" may be a real literature, but it is external evidence B asserted without support from the prompt.
"districts are signing on to expand to 1 million students based on a study" invents district motivation; the update only says the rollout and results are happening together.
"public school teachers" is narrower than the supplied fact of "US school districts" and should not be assumed.
